=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

## Bottom line

The Seller's package is not acceptable as drafted. It combines a low general cap, a deductible basket, short time limits, extended exclusive-remedy and non-reliance protection, general disclosure of the whole data room, and an anti-sandbagging clause (8.3). Together these would leave the Buyer carrying most of the risk for issues it has already identified. Several known liabilities are also left outside the price mechanics or dismissed as "ordinary course." The FINAL label and the "principal-level settlement" language do not bind us. Nothing is agreed until signed, so we should confirm with our principals what, if anything, they actually agreed.

## Key departures from the Buyer's interests

### A. Risk allocation and remedies

| Seller position | Why it hurts us | Buyer pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **Cl 12.1: General cap 20% (AUD 4.8m)** | Top of the Seller's own "market" range. It also caps all general warranties, so one large claim could exhaust it. | Open at 30–40% of price for general warranties. Fallback: 20% only if fundamental, tax, and specific indemnities sit outside it. |
| **Cl 12.2: AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k deductible basket** | The basket is a true deductible (about 1.04% of price), so the first AUD 250k of losses is absorbed by the Buyer. The de minimis excludes small claims entirely, and it is unclear whether those count toward the basket. | Tipping basket (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). Reduce the de minimis to about AUD 10k, and state that below-de-minimis claims aggregate toward the basket. Specific indemnities should be first-dollar and outside both thresholds. |
| **Cl 12.3/13: 18-month limit for general warranties; applies to all Claims** | Eighteen months is too short for a full audit, tax, or year-end cycle. Applying it to all claims would also cut off fundamental and tax claims. | 36 months for general warranties. Fundamental warranties: statutory limitation (six years for contract claims in NSW, confirm with NSW counsel). Tax: statutory assessment period plus a buffer (the ATO amendment period is generally four years, so align accordingly). |
| **Fundamental/title warranties under the same caps and time limits** | Title and capacity warranties are the core of what we are buying. Capping them at AUD 4.8m is wrong. | Cap at 100% of price. Survival to the statutory limitation period. Excluded from basket and de minimis. |
| **Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5: Limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature** | This would cover fraud and could be argued to cover fundamental and tax claims. Contractual exclusion of fraud is generally unenforceable, and statutory protections (including ACL misleading or deceptive conduct protections, where applicable) generally cannot be contracted out of. | Carve out fraud, dishonesty, fundamental warranties, tax indemnity, and specific indemnities. Narrow non-reliance to the extent consistent with law, and confirm the ACL position with NSW counsel. |
| **Cl 8.3: Buyer knowledge bars claims** (anti-sandbagging) | We know about Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the privacy incident, and more. This clause would strip our warranty claims for every known issue. | Delete. Insist on a pro-sandbagging clause: knowledge does not prejudice claims. Known issues should be addressed by specific indemnities, not left to warranty claims. |

### B. Disclosure

- **Cl 1.1 / 1.2 and Schedule 7: general disclosure of the whole data room and public registers.** This effectively discloses everything against every warranty. It also means the Buyer carries diligence risk for documents it cannot realistically read.
  - *Pushback:* Specific disclosure only, against a specific clause, with reasonable detail. No general data room disclosure. Public registers disclosed only where a search result is specifically referenced.
- **Cut-off date.** The data room is frozen at 5pm 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so six weeks of changes are not captured. Require a bring-down and an updated index, with a Seller warranty that nothing material has changed since.
- **Disclosure Letter 1.4 and 11.** These disclaim admissions and state that the Buyer must evaluate facts itself. Acceptable if the rest of the disclosure is narrowed, but they do not reduce our need for specific protection.

### C. Known issues that the Seller has left open

**1. Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, about 30%)**
- Change-control consent (cl 11.2) is not obtained. Conditions in cl 11.3 are not evidenced as satisfied.
- The Seller's draft treats consent as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent." This ignores the cl 11.3 conditions and makes the Seller's obligation only "reasonable endeavours."
- *Pushback:* Written Bluefen consent, including satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions, as a condition precedent. Long-stop date with termination right. If we waive, require a specific indemnity for loss of revenue or termination, plus escrow or price adjustment. Do not accept "reasonable endeavours" as the Seller's only obligation.

**2. Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding, about 13% of price)**
- The facility is not repaid, and the security is not released. The Seller proposes a release "following Completion."
- That would have the Buyer pay the price while the bank retains security over company assets, which is unacceptable. Under a debt-free/cash-free structure, this debt should be deducted from price and paid off at Completion.
- *Pushback:* Payoff letter, release of security and discharge (check PPSR registrations and any guarantees) delivered at Completion. Funds flow to pay Riverlark directly from the price. Confirm the price mechanics show this deduction; the Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics," but we have not seen the reconciliation.

**3. Ironquay Development Studio (IP and SOW3)**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- The Seller's cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and called "adequate." It is not.
- *Pushback:* Ironquay payment (AUD 180k) made by the Seller before Completion or deducted as debt. Confirmatory assignment of all SOW3 Project Materials as a condition precedent. Specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims (unpaid fees, IP ownership, third-party claims, redevelopment costs), outside the cap and basket. Confirm no other SOWs or open invoices.

**4. Employee Completion bonuses (AUD 420k)**
- Not in the funds flow. The disclosure also does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation, or on-costs apply.
- Indicative on-costs (to be verified): NSW payroll tax at around 5.45% is roughly AUD 23k; superannuation at 12% could add up to about AUD 50k if the bonuses are ordinary time earnings. Total cost could be about AUD 490k.
- Conditions include continued employment, so some of the cost may fall on us post-completion.
- *Pushback:* Treat all transaction and Completion bonuses, plus employer on-costs, as debt-like items deducted from price, paid by the Seller or through payroll before Completion. Specific indemnity for any residual claims.

**5. Privacy and data incident (DD-006)**
- About 1,240 records, including names, business emails, roles, and activity timestamps, were sent to an unintended external address. It is not established whether unauthorised access occurred, or whether notification is required.
- If it is an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the company must assess promptly (within 30 days) and notify affected individuals and the OAIC if serious harm is likely. Post-completion, this obligation sits with the company we are buying.
- The Seller calls the matter "not expected to be material" and gives no loss estimate. We should not accept that characterisation.
- *Pushback:* Forensic investigation completed pre-signing or as a condition precedent. Specific indemnity for all incident costs (investigation, notifications, regulatory, third-party claims, remediation), uncapped or separately capped, with long survival. Seller cooperation covenant. Escrow or retention sized to the exposure. Confirm the timing of the 30-day assessment window and the date the company became aware.

**6. Supplier renewals (AUD 330k aggregate, 3 x AUD 110k)**
- The Seller calls them "ordinary-course." The disclosure notes they should be read together for timing and scope, and does not say whether they are unavoidable or terminable. Three near-identical renewals could be one contract split under a threshold.
- *Pushback:* Copies of the contracts and term details. Interim covenant: no new or renewed contracts above a threshold without Buyer consent. Any committed unpaid amounts treated as debt-like, or the price adjusted.

**7. Office lease**
- DD-007 notes a notification obligation but does not say whether landlord consent is required for the share sale.
- *Pushback:* Lease review. If consent or a change-of-control clause applies, landlord consent as a condition precedent, or a specific indemnity.

**8. Mossvale (assignment restriction)**
- The Seller says consent is not required merely because shares are sold.
- *Pushback:* Independent legal review of the clause. If there is any change-of-control trigger, consent becomes a condition precedent. Ask the Seller to confirm in a warranty.

**9. Title (DD-012)**
- The share register shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of shares. The disclosure notes that the Buyer has not verified title independently.
- *Pushback:* Our own verification: ASIC current company extract, original share certificates, constitution (pre-emptive or transfer restrictions), PPSR search over shares, and confirmation of no options or other rights over shares. Fundamental warranty on title and capacity (see A above).

**10. Tax and IP warranties**
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled.
- *Pushback:* Pre-completion tax indemnity, uncapped or capped at price, with statutory limitation survival. IP warranties tailored to the Ironquay and data issues, not general wording.

### D. Counterparty and recovery risk

- **Seller covenant strength.** Harbourglass is a holding entity that may distribute proceeds and become a shell. Any cap is only as good as the Seller's ability to pay.
- **W&I insurance.** Standard W&I policies exclude known matters, so the issues above would fall outside cover. Specific indemnities and escrow or retention are still needed.
- *Pushback:* Retention or escrow for general and specific claims, sized to known exposure. Parent guarantee or a solvency covenant if the Seller is a holding entity.

### E. Drafting and consistency

- Clause references do not reconcile across the Seller Update, SPA, and Disclosure Letter (for example, the incident is "4.6 / Schedule 6" in the update and "section 6" in the letter). Require a clean, reconciled set.
- The disclosure letter is undated, and "as at the date of this letter" has no defined date. Fix this.
- Seller "market context" statements are negotiating assertions, not legal standards. We should not accept them as the benchmark.

## Summary of recommendations

**Immediate (before further negotiation)**
1. Confirm with principals what was actually agreed. Reject the FINAL label and "not to be re-opened" language.
2. Commission forensic review of the privacy incident (DD-006) and a pre-signing legal view on notification obligations.
3. Verify title independently (ASIC, PPSR, share certificates, constitution).
4. Obtain the reconciled funds flow showing Riverlark payoff, bonuses, Ironquay payment, and debt-like items.

**Core SPA positions**
5. General cap: open at 30–40% of price; fallback 20% with fundamental, tax, and specific indemnities outside it.
6. Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority): cap at 100% of price, statutory limitation period.
7. Basket: tipping basket; de minimis reduced to about AUD 10k; specific indemnities first-dollar.
8. Time limits: 36 months general; statutory limitation for fundamental; tax to statutory assessment period plus buffer.
9. Limitations and exclusive remedy: carve out fraud, fundamental, tax, and specific indemnities.
10. Delete cl 8.3 (anti-sandbagging); insert pro-sandbagging clause.
11. Disclosure: specific disclosure only; no general data room or register disclosure; bring-down to a current date.

**Specific protections**
12. Bluefen: written consent including cl 11.3 conditions as condition precedent; long-stop and termination right; specific revenue indemnity if waived.
13. Riverlark: payoff and release at Completion, deducted from price.
14. Ironquay: AUD 180k paid pre-Completion or deducted; confirmatory assignment as condition precedent; specific uncapped indemnity.
15. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as debt-like items.
16. Privacy incident: forensic review; specific indemnity; cooperation covenant; escrow or retention.
17. Supplier renewals: contract review; interim covenant on new commitments; committed amounts as debt-like or price adjustment.
18. Lease and Mossvale: legal review; consents as condition precedent if triggered.
19. Tax and IP: specific tax indemnity; tailored IP warranties.

**Security for recovery**
20. Retention or escrow sized to known exposures.
21. Seller solvency covenant or parent guarantee.
22. Consider W&I, recognising known-matter exclusions mean specific protections are still required.

**Caveats**
- Figures are indicative. Payroll tax and superannuation estimates need confirmation from the Buyer's tax advisers.
- Statutory references (Privacy Act notification timing, Limitation Act periods, ACL application to B2B share sales, and the ATO amendment period) should be confirmed by NSW and tax counsel before we rely on them in the mark-up.
